main_text.p: confilium à desperatione sumptum: bellum unanimi consensu decretum, arma nova summo studio fabrefacta, classis festinato opere constructa, in usum machinarum capilli fœminarum detonsi, & in funes conversi. Tum secutā, quæ excidium urbis superius à me expositum traxerunt.

Res Carthaginis veteris brevissimè constrinxit Iustinus ex Trogo Pompeio, fusius scripsit Diodorus Siculus exorsus à sæculo Xerxis, prolixissimè recitarunt recentiora ejus Polybius & Livius. Claros belli duces Carthago multos habuit præter eos quos in hoc commentario de republicâ ejus recensui. Plerorumque istorum nomina & memoriam cum brevissimis actorum & eventuum notis recolui in serie genealogicá principum Punicorum[?], quæ cum cæteris regum, principum, procerum, qui diversis in gentibus floruêre, genealogiis à me editis, & operi chronologico adjunctis extat. Ad quam seriem lectores cognoscendi cupidos remitto. Bella gravia vario eventu Carthaginenses gessere contra Afros, Numidas, Mauros in ipsa Africâ: contra Græcos & Barbaros in Siciliâ, contra Sardos indigenas in Sardiniâ, contra Hispanos in Hispania, harumq; regionum

page.notes: Catchword "num" is printed at the lower right. The marks after "Punicorum" and "genealogicá" are doubtful: the scan shows a dash-like sign after "Punicorum", which I have not reproduced, so the word is marked [?]. The long s has been written as plain s throughout. The "ff" ligature in "brevissimè", "prolixissimè", "fcripfit" and similar words has been read as ss. Ornamental marks at the lower left and the right edge of the neighbouring page are not transcribed.
